transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… people at work say I’m hard to follow lately. Like when I’m trying to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts coming out mixed up—trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone… all kind of jumps around. Then they look at me like they don’t know what I’m talking about.
Have you been feeling unusually energized lately?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think so. I’ve just been trying to get through work, same as usual.
Do you know what day it is today?
I’m… not totally sure. I think it’s a weekday, but I’d have to check.
Can you tell me where you are right now?
I’m not sure… I think I’m in a doctor’s office. Here, I guess.
Are you having trouble focusing on what people are saying to you?
I don’t know… maybe a little sometimes. I can usually follow, but I might need a second.
Are you seeing things that other people do not seem to see?
I… don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed, anyway.
Did this confusion come on suddenly?
No… not suddenly. It’s been kind of building up, I guess. Maybe around 11 months… since the new district manager started pushing harder on forecasts and schedules.
Do you feel that anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?
No… I don’t think anyone’s trying to hurt me. I mean, people at work can be difficult, but… plotting against me? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say that.
Do you have times when you feel much more drowsy or much more alert than usual?
I’m not sure. I get tired sometimes, sure, but I haven’t really noticed big swings like that… not much more than usual.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, sometimes it’s quiet and I’m tired, but I haven’t noticed voices when nobody’s there.
Have you been diagnosed with a medical or brain condition?
Not that I know of. I mean… nothing like a brain condition that I’ve been told about.
Have you been having trouble managing your usual daily activities?

Yeah… some. Work’s been harder. They don’t really let me run the busy weekend shifts anymore, and after my review my boss said I could be suspended if I don’t get things back in order.

At home, my wife’s had to pick up some things I used to handle. People were getting… uncomfortable, I guess, or confused around me.
Have people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to?
I’m not sure. Nobody’s really said it to me like that… at least not that I remember.
Do there are times during the day when you feel much more confused than at other times?
I don’t know… not really. Some parts of the day feel more off than others, maybe, but I haven’t kept track of it or anything.
Have you been feeling less motivated to do things than you used to?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really noticed that specifically. I still do what I have to, mostly.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?
I don’t know… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed anything big.
Have you started using any new drugs or medicines in the past year?
No, I don’t think so. Nothing new that I can remember.
Are you having trouble paying attention?
I’m not sure. I mean, sometimes my mind wanders, but I haven’t really thought of it as a problem.
Do you believe people are sending you special messages through the television, radio, or other things around you?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve noticed things on TV sometimes, but I wouldn’t say they’re messages to me. Not really.
Have you been seeing things that other people cannot see?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I might think I see something out of the corner of my eye, but nothing I’d really say is… seeing things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview primarily shows confusion/disorientation and disorganized, hard-to-follow speech with impaired functioning, but without clear evidence of persistent delusions, hallucinations, or a known medical condition causing psychosis. He is not oriented to day and is only partially oriented to place, and coworkers describe him as difficult to follow. Because psychotic symptoms are not clearly established, schizophrenia and unspecified psychosis are less supported. A medical psychotic disorder is also not supported because no medical/brain condition is known. Among the provided options, confusion/disorientation is the best fit.
